recipes.name: Homemade Blueberry Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) with oven rack in lowest position.
Combine sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl; sprinkle over blueberries in a separate bowl.

Line a 9-inch pie plate with 1 pie crust. Pour berry mixture into crust; dot with butter. Cut remaining pie crust into ½- to ¾-inch-wide strips. Moisten the rim of the pie with a small amount of water. Start with the longest strips and lay the first 2 in an X in the center of the pie. Alternate horizontal and vertical strips, weaving them in an over-and-under pattern. Use the shortest strips for the edges of the lattice. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and flute the crust.
Bake in the preheated oven on the lowest oven rack until filling is bubbling and crust is golden brown, about 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Blueberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: This blueberry pie has a juicy filling made with fresh blueberries and a gorgeous lattice pastry crust for a sweet summer dessert that's hard to beat.

video.description: Make a delicious fresh blueberry pie, complete with lattice crust.

review.reviewBody: This pie is very yummy! I would only changed a couple of things. I put 5 level Tablespoons of cornstarch instead of the 3 TBSP. I also added 2 TBSP of lemon juice. I would advise changing the oven temperature to 375 degrees because even after covering the edge of the crust it still got a little overdone on 425 degrees. I would also not cook it on the bottom rack, but the middle rack. Finally, wait at least 1 hour before cutting to let the cornstarch do its thing or you will end up with to much juice. FRESH BLUEBERRYS ARE THE TICKET!!! AGAIN, VERY YUMMY!!! (loved it with vanialla ice cream)!

I'm giving this four stars because I had to tweak it some. I used 5 cups of blueberries, 6 tbsp of cornstarch and 1 1/4 c sugar, lowered the heat to 400 and it was perfect! The first one I made, I followed the recipe to a tee, except increased the cornstarch to 5 tbsp (per several other reviews) and baked at 425. It was very runny and it burned.

Perfect. We found that this is a tart-sweet pie with the juices gelled just enough not to run out of the pie IF you use a lattice crust and very small fresh blueberries.
If you are making a solid top crust, or using cultivated "high bush berries", increase the cornstarch by 1 TBSP for each change. 
The 3/4 cup sugar can be increased to 1 cup for those who prefer a sweeter pie, but you'll need a bit more cornstarch since more sugar draws more juice out of the berries. 
I personally found the cooking time is accurate for a lattice top, but I had to lower the temp to 400 and increase the baking time to about 1 hour for a full top crust. 
Browning time on a crust varies widely. Crusts with more fat, or that use butter as some/all of the fat will brown more quickly than a crust with less fat or all shortening/oil.
Be sure to try this pie with sharp cheddar cheese. There's a reason New Englanders eat pie for breakfast!

This is an excellant pie! I have made 5 since I got it. I have used fresh blueberries and frozen blueberries. They both work great. The one thing I did different was that I added 5 cups of blueberries because I used my deep dish pie baker from Pampered Chef. I also followed the advice to us 5 tbs. constarch. As an added tip for everyone, I used, "Basic Flaky Pie Crust" sumitted by Stephanie. A wonderful pie crust. Everyone loved it and said it was the best Blueberry pie they had ever eaten. Crust and all. Thank you Beth and Stephanie! The two of you make a winning combination!

I loved this pie recipe! It was super-easy to make, and it was delicious! After reading the other reviews, I put in 4 tbsp of cornstarch instead of 3 tbsp, and it set without a problem. Also, I added a splash of lemon juice to the blueberry mixture for some extra flavor, and I covered the edges of the pie crust with aluminum foil until the last 15 minutes (to prevent overbrowning). A great recipe!

I altered the recipe slightly as other people had suggested. I did 5 Tbsp of cornstarch, 1 Tbsp of lemon juice and added 1/2 top of vanilla extract along with the other ingredients. I also buttered the pie tin to prevent the crust from sticking. I baked at 375 on the center rack for 50 minutes in my conventional oven, allowed it to cool and it set beautifully even at room temperature. If you have a convection oven (where the air/heat is circulating in the oven reduce the temperature to 350 and the cook time will change). Lastly, I egg washed the top crust to give it that nice shine. Happy baking.

I used store bought frozen blueberries, and added the ingredients, bumping up the cornstarch to 6 Tbsp. adding the 2 tsp lemon juice, and split the cinnamon to 1/4 and 1/4 nutmeg and 1 tsp vanilla. I let the berries warm to room temp in my mixing bowl. By the time they warmed up there was a lot of liquid, so I strained off about 1.5 - 2 cups of syrup, and precooked it in a sauce pan. ( I was worried that the uncooked liquid would make the crust soggy) I added the berries to my pie shell, and topped off with the syrup after it had cooled before placing the top crust. Turned out great.

I made the following changes, but other than having to make these changes, the original recipe was as good Betty Crocker’s cookbook recipe. Changes: Bake at 400F for 50 minutes or until blueberry filling is bubbling up thru the cuts in the top crust, on center rack in oven, removing the foil (or silicone edge protector from the edge of pie crust after the first 40 minutes of baking. The bubbling means it got hot enough to meld with the flour or cornstarch and the filling won’t be runny if you let it cool. Cool for at least an hour for the blueberry filling to set. 3/4 cup sugar 1/2 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon 6 cups fresh blueberries 1 tablespoon lemon juice 2 tablespoons butter, cut into little pieces. Photo is pie with silicone edge protector before I put the pie in the oven.

It's a good recipe, but 4 stars b/c I had to tweak it. I used 5 cups of blueberries (C'mon! Gimme a good, full piece of pie!) and slightly adjusted the dry ingredients accordingly. I also put a cookie sheet in the oven, which I preheated to 425. I put the pie in the oven for 10 minutes, then lowered it to 375 for about 40-45 minutes. I find that technique helps to prevent pies with a "soggy bottom". I also find that the black bird steamer helps with this. This was for July 4th, so I used my cookie cutter and made the top crust all stars. Gave it an egg wash and sprinkled Demerara sugar for a bit of sparkle and crunch. One pie was finished last night (7/3). I had to hide the second for dessert 7/4.

Just made this for Christmas Eve, and it was a hit with everyone! I followed this recipe down to a tee, but one change that I made that I absolutely recommend is adding lemon juice. It does a phenomenal job of bringing out the flavor of the blueberries, and the pie has a nice tangy and tart taste as a result. I squeezed the juice of at least one lemon and strained the juice with a sieve. After the dry ingredients are mixed in with the blueberries, I poured in two tablespoons of the lemon juice into the mixture and folded it all in with a rubber spatula. Then I left it to set for at least an hour (the longer the better) before baking as directed to have the blueberries absorb all of the flavors. I hope this helps!

Great base recipe. I made a few tweaks: -Used 4 scant cups (so more like 3 1/3) of fresh blueberries and dropped the sugar to 1/2 cup. I heeded the advice of others to increase the cornstarch to 4 tbsp. I also added 1/4 tsp of coriander power in lieu of the cinnamon I then added 1/2 of a lemon and all of the zest. I think next time I’d macerate the fruit in the sugar for an hours and then add the rest. After dotting with butter, I baked at 425 for about 1 hour and then dropped the temp to 375 for 15 more minutes. Fruit had nicely set and wasn’t dry either.

The filling didn’t set. I followed the recipe to the letter and the filling is just soup. It tastes good though but the entire reason I chose this recipe is that the reviews were good and the picture looked like the filling set well.
I’ve made this several times and my family loves it!
Love it! Simple and delicious. Worth the extra effort to make the pie crust from scratch.
I really liked this recipe I added some lemon and it was nice and tart.
Easy to make with great results!

I came to see this recipe after I made mine and just wanted to see what temperature to bake it on since I forgot exactly how I did it last time. I first looked at couple of recipes and then, I did my own thing anyway. So I use 2 1/2 large spoons of almond flour so the blueberries do not run over the pie plate. It comes out really delicious. Also I always use vanilla extract and one packet of vanilla sugar that you can buy on amazon if you do not have a European deli near by. So now I have to watch my pie since it is in a new oven, and I am planning to cover the edges after half hour of baking.
Its great I made it for my family and they all loved it

Terrible recipe. After raising the temperature to over 400 and baking for an additional 30 minutes it still wasn’t bubbly and there were clumps of sugar and cornstarch that had not dissolved to form juice and thicken. I wasted $14.00 worth of beautiful blueberries. This is the last one I’ll ever make from Allrecipes.

I followed the recipe precisely. I used fresh organic blueberries, 4 cups. Baked at 375 per recipe. Well, the blueberry pie was way too runny and difficult to serve. Should I have used more cornstarch than what the recipe called for? I'm not giving up on blueberry pie-making, but I won't use this recipe next time.
